findings.evidence: `upstream/Physlib/Physlib/Relativity/Tensors/RealTensor/Vector/Basic.lean:414` `def ofTemporalComponent ... toFun xt := xt • basis (Sum.inl 0)` and `:421` `def ofSpatialComponent ... toFun xs := ∑ i, xs i • basis (Sum.inr i)`; the PR's raw spelling at `BasicExtensions.lean:38` and `Continuation/Basic.lean:338`, with the component facts at `BasicExtensions.lean:41-45`.
findings.fix: State the projection as `v - ofTemporalComponent v.timeComponent` (or `ofSpatialComponent v.spatialPart`), or add the bridge lemma `v - v.timeComponent • basis (Sum.inl 0) = ofSpatialComponent v.spatialPart`; and expose the two component facts as public `@[simp]` lemmas (`timeComponent_sub_timeComponent_smul_basis`, `spatialPart_sub_timeComponent_smul_basis`) rather than leaving them inline.
findings.issue: The equal-time projection is published as the raw term `v - v.timeComponent • basis (Sum.inl 0)` in two public statements (here and `QFT/Lattice/Continuation/Basic.lean:337`), although Physlib already names both pieces: `Lorentz.Vector.ofTemporalComponent xt = xt • basis (Sum.inl 0)` and `ofSpatialComponent`. Nothing links the two spellings, so these lemmas do not apply to a projection written the canonical upstream way, and the facts that characterize the projection — `timeComponent (v - v.timeComponent • basis (Sum.inl 0)) = 0` and `spatialPart (…) = v.spatialPart` — exist only as `have h₀`/`have hsp` inside this proof (lines 41-45), forcing every later consumer (e.g. Layer 0.3's boundary statements) to reprove them.

findings.evidence: `Continuation/Basic.lean:193-213` exposes only `euclideanSection_def` and the component-form `mem_euclideanSection_iff`; `Uniqueness.lean:104` and `:109` both do `rw [SetLike.mem_coe, euclideanSection_def]`.
findings.fix: Add to `Continuation/Basic.lean` a `@[simp] theorem continuation_mem_euclideanSection (x : EuclideanSeparation d) : continuation x ∈ euclideanSection d` and the matching elimination `mem_euclideanSection_iff_exists_continuation {z} : z ∈ euclideanSection d ↔ ∃ x, continuation x = z`, and use them here instead of `euclideanSection_def`.
findings.issue: `euclideanSection` has no introduction lemma in terms of the map that defines it, so the first consumer of the section must unfold `euclideanSection_def` and apply `LinearMap.mem_range_self` to produce `continuation x ∈ euclideanSection d` (also at line 104 for the elimination direction). Every downstream user of `eqOn_of_eqOn_euclideanSection`, which takes `EqOn f g (U ∩ euclideanSection d)`, hits the same step.

summary: The Wick-rotation API and the new identity theorem are well-formed and correctly exposed, but the "equal-time projection" is published under an ad-hoc term spelling that bypasses Physlib's existing `ofTemporalComponent`/`ofSpatialComponent`, with its two characterizing component facts buried inside a proof; and `euclideanSection` still has no introduction lemma for `continuation`, so the PR's own first consumer unfolds the definition.
